item.title: Pharmacy Plus PEI marks four-year anniversary
item.description:
Pharmacy Plus PEI marks four-year anniversary jenniferdhogan Wed, 10/28/2026 - 10:23

This month marks the fourth anniversary of Pharmacy Plus PEI, with more than 91, 800 Islanders having accessed over 309,500 assessments since the program began.

The Pharmacy Plus PEI program supports 48 participating pharmacies in 15 communities across the province to renew eligible prescriptions and assess and prescribe for 35 common ailments and conditions. 

“Every day, Islanders are receiving timely care close to home through Pharmacy Plus PEI.  Since its inception, more than $6.67 million worth of direct patient care has been provided through the program.  I want to thank pharmacists across the Island for the important service they provide in their communities. Their dedication to patient care has made this program a success.”

- Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle

Since its launch, participating pharmacies have provided a range of assessment and prescribing services including the following (as of Oct. 15, 2026):  

  • Over 197,360 prescription renewal assessments (63.8 per cent of all Pharmacy Plus assessments)
  • Over 21,800 urinary tract infection assessments (7 per cent)
  • Over 9,400 allergic rhinitis assessments (3 per cent)
  • Over 7,400 cough assessments (2.4 per cent)
  • Over 5,800 nasal congestion assessments (1.87 per cent)
  • Over 1,400 contraception assessments (since the service expanded in July 2023)

The program also expanded in December 2025 to include strep throat testing and treatment as part of sore throat assessments. More than 2,900 Islanders have accessed the service to date, helping divert patients from emergency departments and other primary health care settings.

“The Pharmacy Plus Program has demonstrated that an investment in pharmacy services results in increased access to health care,” said PEI Pharmacy Association executive director Erin MacKenzie. “We look forward to ongoing conversations, focused on expanding our scope of care through sustainable models that protect and enhance patient access”.

For more information, visit Pharmacy Plus PEI

item.title: Paving the way for the next generation of Island women in medicine
item.description:
Paving the way for the next generation of Island women in medicine jenniferdhogan Wed, 10/28/2026 - 09:53

For five Island women, studying medicine means being part of something new: the opportunity to pursue their medical education at home in Prince Edward Island. 

Meghan Kiley, Lauren Reid, Hannah Fong, Monica Gollaher, and Sydney Riggs are part of the first cohort of the Memorial regional campus medical learners at the University of Prince Edward Island. While each has her own story and path to medicine, they share a desire to make a difference in the lives of others. 

For Meghan, studying medicine at home carries special meaning. 

“Growing up on the Island, attending medical school here was never an option,” Meghan says.  “Being able to pursue my education in the same communities that helped shape who I am is especially meaningful.” 

For Lauren, being part of the first cohort means setting an example for future students of what medical education looks like on PEI. 

“When I applied there were no medical students studying on PEI, which made it challenging to connect with peers who understood the journey,” says Lauren. “Now I feel fortunate to be in a position where I can provide that guidance and support to other Island women interested in pursuing medicine.” 

Their experiences also highlight the importance of women’s representation in health care, both in patient care and leadership. 

Hannah sees learning from women already leading in Island health care as an opportunity to help build a system that better reflects the needs of the people it serves. 

“Having more women in medicine brings more attention, research, and funding to women’s health issues,” Hannah says. “Having more representation in health care leadership means more women at the table when important decisions are made.” 

Sydney brings a unique perspective through her previous experience in health care finance and governance at Health PEI. 

“I saw firsthand that the people around the table shape which questions get asked and which priorities get funded,” Sydney says. “More women in health care leadership positions means those decisions better reflect the patients and workforce they affect.” 

Meghan says having more female physicians on PEI is an important step towards addressing gaps in women’s health research and care. 

“Greater representation will lead to a more inclusive health care system where women feel heard, supported, and equally represented,” she says. 

All five women also recognize the impact of the people who supported them along the way. Each can point to mothers, mentors, coaches, professors, friends, and colleagues who showed them what is possible and encouraged them to pursue their goals. 

Now, they have an opportunity to offer that same encouragement to others. 

“I hope girls growing up in PEI know that being from a small province doesn’t have to limit what they can do or what they want to achieve,” Monica says.

As they continue their medical education, these five women hope to help make that future more visible for the next generation of Island women… showing them that they can pursue ambitious careers, contribute to their communities, and build lives that reflect their own goals. 

Throughout October, the Government of Prince Edward Island is celebrating Women’s History Month by highlighting Island women whose experiences, achievements, and leadership are helping shape the future of their communities and inspiring the next generation.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
